paragraphs: The London Borough of Bexley runs its own fostering service, shown above with the independent agencies that list Bexley as an area they cover. The council welcomes single people and couples, people who work, and people who rent as well as those who own their home; no qualifications are needed because training is provided.

Bexley asks that applicants are over 21, live in the UK full time or have permission to remain, are in good general health and have the time and space to care for a child. A criminal record or a health condition does not automatically rule you out, but the council asks you to be open about it from the start. If you rent or have a mortgage, you sign a consent form so your landlord or lender can be checked.

The route in is an enquiry and information pack, an information session (online, in person or a one-to-one visit), then a home visit and an application pack that includes a full GP medical, which the council pays for. Statutory checks follow, including DBS checks for everyone in the household aged 16 or over, and a social worker assesses you over a few months, including the Skills to Foster course. Your report then goes to the fostering panel, and the final decision is made by the council's agency decision maker.

Approved Bexley carers get a supervising social worker, a mentor who is an experienced foster carer, a 24-hour duty phone line all year, support groups and coffee mornings, groups for the children in fostering families, and a personal development programme. Carers are also represented by the Bexley Foster Care Association.
Talk to the council and to two or three of the services above, and compare what each offers in pay, training and support.
